observations.text: SP, due to a late break flown with insufficient bank and no correction of the resulting downwind spacing, did not place the A/C in downwind within the prescribed parameters, with the result that downwind altitude was 380 feet low against the +/-150 feet standard and airspeed decayed below the 120 KIAS minimum. The IP directed the corrections and flew part of the base leg to re-establish the roll-out point. Further practice in break zone geometry and in downwind energy management is required.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern, did not plan the final as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and converged on the final, with the result that final altitude was 260 feet high against the +100/-50 feet standard and the A/C was not aligned with the RWY centerline at 1/2 NM prior to the RWY threshold. The IP took control on base leg to re-establish the roll-out point and directed the go around. The pattern could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to an imprecise roll-out point computation on base leg, did not establish the final without deviation from the extended RWY centerline, with the result that final airspeed reached the +15 knot limit and final altitude reached the +200 feet limit of the standard. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, only after the IP's verbal prompts. No IP intervention on the controls was required and no stall characteristics developed.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not maintain the downwind parameters after the landing gear and flap configuration change, with the result that downwind airspeed reached the +20 knot limit and downwind altitude reached 300 feet high, at the outer limit of the standard. Recognition was late and the correction was applied only after the IP's verbal prompt. The required checks and the standardized downwind report were completed after being called for.

SP, due to a delayed power reduction after the break, did not contain the downwind parameters within the desired band, with the result that downwind airspeed exceeded the standard by 16 knots and downwind altitude deviated 220 feet high. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. The break itself was executed within the break zone, with ATC clearance and after clearing the downwind.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not hold the briefed bank on the break while completing the required checks, with the result of a 13 degree bank deviation against the +/-10 degree standard and a base leg airspeed 15 knots above the standard. Both deviations were self-detected and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention. The A/C was aligned with the RWY centerline prior to 1/2 NM from the RWY threshold and no stall characteristics developed.

SP performed the overhead pattern within the desired standards, executing the break within the break zone with ATC clearance and placing the A/C in downwind with the minimum airspeed of 120 KIAS. Downwind altitude was held within 130 feet and final airspeed within 8 knots of the standard; however, both parameters drifted to the high side and required correction twice, and the roll-out point was adjusted late on base leg. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in break spacing and in base leg planning is expected to improve.

SP executed the overhead pattern with exceptional accuracy, placing the break within the break zone with ATC clearance and after clearing the downwind, and holding downwind altitude, airspeed and bank with negligible deviations. Final was planned from an accurate roll-out point, with no deviation or convergence from the final and with alignment on the RWY centerline well prior to 1/2 NM from the RWY threshold. All required checks were completed and the standardized reports were given without prompting, with full adherence to the landing gear and flap limitations. Above end of block MIF achieved.
